event: Crusader army crushed at Varna
description: An Ottoman army defeats the last major western crusade in the region.
strategic_effect: Removed the last sizeable western field army and left Byzantium without realistic relief prospects.
conflict_note: Only the year is given in the retrieved source.

event: Mehmed II begins his second reign
description: Mehmed II (reigned 1444-46 and 1451-81) returns to the throne in 1451.
strategic_effect: Brought to power a sultan who made the capture of Constantinople his defining project.

event: Mehmed II resolves to attack Constantinople
description: The Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium dates his resolve to attack to as early as autumn 1451.
strategic_effect: Starts an approximately 18-month preparation window before the siege opens (computed from dates).

event: Work begins on Rumeli Hisari at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus
description: A fortress is raised opposite Anadolu Hisari (built 1393-94) where the strait is about 660 m wide.
strategic_effect: Let the Ottomans control shipping between the Black Sea and the city.
conflict_note: Sphrantzes says the sultan occupied the straits on 26 March 1452; the Limen Project gives 15 April for the start of construction. Archnet says only 'spring 1452'.

event: Rumeli Hisari completed after about four and a half months
description: Sphrantzes records that once the castle was complete the sultan left on 31 August 1452.
strategic_effect: Completed the Bosphorus chokepoint a full winter before the siege.

event: Venetian ship destroyed while running the Bosphorus
description: A Venetian ship that ignored the ban on traffic is sunk by the fortress guns and its captain executed (as reported).
strategic_effect: Demonstrated that the new fortress could close the strait to shipping.
conflict_note: Single popular source.

event: Union of the Churches proclaimed in Hagia Sophia
description: Act of union with the Latin church celebrated in Hagia Sophia in an effort to secure western aid.
strategic_effect: Did not produce timely military help and deepened internal religious division (contested).
conflict_note: Date and framing follow standard narratives (Runciman; Nicol); not independently checked in the sources retrieved for this project.

event: Hagia Sophia converted into an imperial mosque (name retained)
description: Necipoglu: converted in 1453 into the premier imperial mosque of the city, keeping the name Ayasofya.
strategic_effect: Symbolic and practical assertion of Ottoman religious authority in the old centre.

event: Mehmed II formally announces the attack
description: The Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium says he officially proclaimed his intent only in January 1453.
strategic_effect: Moves the plan from private decision to declared war aim.

event: Giovanni Giustiniani Longo arrives with a small professional contingent
description: A Genoese commander reinforces the defence (about 700 men in popular accounts).
strategic_effect: Added experienced troops, but small in absolute terms against the length of the walls.
conflict_note: Numbers come from a popular source only.

event: Limited western relief: two Venetian ships and 800 men
description: World History Encyclopedia says Venice sent two ships and 800 men in April 1453, Genoa promised another ship and the Pope later promised five armed ships, but the Ottomans had already blockaded the city.
strategic_effect: Relief was small and late; the defence stood largely alone.
conflict_note: Single popular source for the numbers.

event: Boom stretched across the Golden Horn
description: The defenders close the harbour mouth with a chain.
strategic_effect: Protected the weaker Golden Horn sea walls from direct naval assault.

event: Mehmed II arrives with the main army
description: The sultan and the remaining detachments take position before the walls.
strategic_effect: Completes the encirclement of the land front.
conflict_note: World History Encyclopedia says the army assembled on 2 April; Sphrantzes says the sultan returned and laid siege on 4 April.

event: Siege formally opens and bombardment begins
description: Conventional start date of the siege in the Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium.
strategic_effect: Starts the roughly 53-day siege clock (elapsed days to 29 May).
conflict_note: Sphrantzes gives 4 April.

event: Ottoman fleet's first attempt on the boom fails
description: The Ottoman fleet attacks the chain and fails to break it.
strategic_effect: Showed the boom held against direct assault.
conflict_note: Popular sources vary between 9 and 12 April.

event: First major infantry assault on the walls repelled
description: An assault on the damaged Lycus-valley section is driven back.
strategic_effect: The defenders' inner lines remained intact despite cannon damage.
conflict_note: Single popular source.

event: Outer wall in the Lycus valley destroyed; defenders build a stockade
description: The Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium says that within a fortnight of 6 April large cannons cast by Urbinus destroyed the outer wall in the Lycus valley and the defenders built a stockade in front of the inner wall.
strategic_effect: Artillery reduced a two-line defence to one line at the most critical sector.
conflict_note: Date is approximate: 'within a fortnight'.

event: Four Christian ships break through the blockade into the Golden Horn
description: Three Genoese vessels and one Byzantine ship fight through to the harbour.
strategic_effect: Lifted defender morale and showed the limits of the Ottoman naval blockade.

event: Ottoman ships hauled overland into the Golden Horn
description: The Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium records the penetration of the Golden Horn on 22 April; about 70 ships are reported.
strategic_effect: Forced the defenders to guard the Golden Horn sea walls as a second front with the same small force.

event: Allied night attack on the Ottoman ships in the Golden Horn fails
description: An attempt to destroy the transferred ships is repulsed.
strategic_effect: Left the Ottoman fleet in the harbour.
conflict_note: Single popular source.

event: Venetian ships return with news that no relief is coming
description: Popular summaries report a small Venetian squadron returning to tell Constantine no relief force is on its way.
strategic_effect: Removed the last realistic hope of outside help.
conflict_note: Date is approximate in popular sources.

event: Grand vizier Halil Pasha counsels ending the siege
description: The Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium records that on 25 May the vizier advised retreat.
strategic_effect: Shows the outcome was still contested inside the Ottoman camp four days before the fall.

event: Final assault begins at about 01:30
description: Tuesday 29 May; the Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium describes two futile charges over about four hours.
strategic_effect: Opened a single, concentrated push on the land front.

event: Janissaries breach the stockade near the Gate of St. Romanus
description: Towards dawn Janissaries break through the stockade and climb the inner wall.
strategic_effect: First decisive breach on the land front.

event: Kerkoporta postern reported unattended at Blachernae
description: About an hour later the defence cracks at two points; a small band slips through the Kerkoporta.
strategic_effect: Created a second breakthrough point in the northern sector.
conflict_note: Popular retellings of a gate left open are debated.

event: Giustiniani wounded and defensive cohesion weakens
description: Popular sources describe the wounding of the Genoese commander during the assault.
strategic_effect: May have disrupted command at a critical moment.
conflict_note: Timing and circumstances vary between accounts.

event: Constantine XI killed in the fighting
description: The Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium says he fell in battle shortly after the defence cracked; the details of his death and burial are unknown.
strategic_effect: End of the Byzantine imperial line.
conflict_note: The fact of his death is well supported; circumstances are not.

event: Mehmed II enters the city and processes to Hagia Sophia
description: By noon most of the city was taken; in the afternoon the sultan led a procession to Hagia Sophia; looting continued into the evening.
strategic_effect: Marks the transfer of control of the city.
conflict_note: Some accounts name Edirnekapi as the gate of entry.

event: Mehmed II leaves the city; first repopulation attempt falters by autumn
description: Oz reports that settlers brought from Anatolia had gone back home by the time the sultan returned in the autumn.
strategic_effect: Repopulation needed sustained coercion and incentives, not a single transfer.

event: George Scholarios (Gennadios II) appointed Orthodox patriarch
description: Oz dates the appointment to 6 January 1454.
strategic_effect: The Orthodox patriarchate continued under Ottoman authority.

event: First Ottoman survey of Istanbul and Galata completed
description: The 1455 survey records households, not individuals; the surviving copy is partial (33 Istanbul quarters, 23 Galata quarters, 864 Galata households).
strategic_effect: Created the first administrative baseline for the new capital.

event: Settlers from Serbian Hungarian and Bulgarian lands moved to the city surroundings
description: As reported by Kritovoulos and cited by Oz.
strategic_effect: Part of a wider resettlement (surgun) policy.

event: Hagia Sophia endowment deed drawn up
description: Oz notes the waqf deed of Hagia Sophia was arranged in 1457.
strategic_effect: Endowments financed the conversion of old religious buildings.

event: Yedikule Fortress built behind the Golden Gate
description: Ottoman citadel added at the Marmara end of the land walls.
strategic_effect: Kept the old fortifications useful in Ottoman hands.
conflict_note: Single secondary source.

event: Capital formally moved from Edirne to Istanbul
description: Necipoglu dates Mehmed II's strategic move of the capital to 1459, citing Kritoboulos.
strategic_effect: Made the city the permanent centre of the Ottoman state.
conflict_note: Popular accounts often say 1453; Necipoglu says 1459.

event: New Palace (Topkapi) begun; completion inscription dated 1478
description: Construction began in 1459 on the old acropolis; an inscription on the Imperial Gate dates completion to 1478.
strategic_effect: New administrative core for the state.

event: Former residents permitted to return; Morea population resettled (1459-60)
description: Reported by Oz.
strategic_effect: Combined incentives with forced transfer.

event: Fatih Mosque complex built on the site of the Church of the Holy Apostles
description: Foundation inscription dated 1463-70; eight madrasas; construction was initiated in 1459 according to Necipoglu.
strategic_effect: Created a new religious and educational centre and anchor for urban growth.
conflict_note: Start dated 1459 (initiated) versus 1463 (inscription).

event: Major plague strikes; over 600 dead reported
description: Oz notes the city nevertheless saw large population growth within the following decade.
strategic_effect: Recovery was punctuated by shocks.

event: Tiled Kiosk (Cinili Kosk) completed
description: Completed in 1472 (877 AH) according to Necipoglu.
strategic_effect: Part of the palace-building programme.

event: Household census of Istanbul and Galata
description: The register records 16,324 households (see population_1477_households).
strategic_effect: Provides the first solid quantitative anchor after the conquest.
conflict_note: S18 gives 16,326 households, two more than the register table.

event: Fatih complex endowed with commercial establishments; gold coinage from 1477-78
description: Necipoglu notes the endowments were furnished with shops and other commercial establishments and that a gold coin was minted from 1477-78.
strategic_effect: Tied the new capital's finances to endowed commerce and coinage.

event: Ottoman-Venetian peace treaty; Gentile Bellini resident in Istanbul 1479-81
description: Necipoglu links the treaty to Venetian privileges and to Bellini's stay.
strategic_effect: Restored commercial diplomacy with a former opponent.

event: Death of Mehmed II
description: Necipoglu gives 3 May 1481.
strategic_effect: Ends the founding reign of the Ottoman capital.
